author: Yffe
content: Pin: §4 'The chosen form' displays the resolution clause as an ANTECEDENT: '(∀ name ∈ calledSpecFns(item), env.specs name ≠ none) → reqDenote … → denote fuel ens = True'. Two readings, both defective. (A) As literally written, ∀ (env : Env) quantifies env.specs too — then the hypothesis only requires names resolve to SOME SpecFn, never pinning the REAL bodies, so the obligation quantifies over wrong-body registries (unprovable wrong statement) and is incoherent with EXP's 'the EXPORTED Env.specs registry'. (B) Intended reading (concrete exported registry, value-bindings quantified): the hypothesis is a closed decidable proposition about the emitted registry; an exporter that OMITS a called spec-fn makes it FALSE and the whole obligation is provable from the false premise — a registry-population bug self-certifies kernel-clean. The only guard the doc gives is EXP arm-by-arm INSPECTION ('paired with EXP registry faithfulness'), i.e. the trust item whose failure mode IS the omission. Sound alternatives the doc did not choose: (a) exporter-side hard gate — export FAILS mechanically when calledSpecFns(item) ⊄ dom(registry), so the theorem never carries the premise; (b) decide/rfl-discharged resolution lemmas emitted alongside (omission fails to compile). Secondary: the soundness paragraph's claim (1) 'every specCall … is fully unfolded at every fuel in range, so the => True arm is NEVER taken' is false for recursive spec-fns (static nesting depth ≠ value-dependent unfolding depth; Denote.lean: body 'MAY contain further specCalls'), though the ∀-fuel form itself stays sound. fuel₀ under-computation verified NOT soundness-bearing (the doc's parenthetical is correct).
